feature: Marketing Buy / Checkout page (/buy) — the one checkout for all three products. Asserts the product-specific rules that make or break the flow: monitoring gates pricing+payment behind a tenant connection, retainer offers a skippable scan and is never gated, packs are multi-select with a summed one-time total, and the terms checkbox gates the pay button without ever hiding the payment fields.

notes: Git #4383 (sessionTag 4383-account-first): Retainer runs account -> connect (optional, still skippable) -> tier &
pay -> portal. /buy?product=retainer opens on the same identity step as Monitoring and Packs; the buying screen
(tier, the optional connect card with its Skip button, pay) only renders once the account has a password and MFA.
The consent URL for a Retainer session is refused server-side (409 account_required) until then; the skip
(read-consent-skip) needs no consent and is unchanged, so a buyer who never connects still pays and ends at
RetainerPending. A tier change after the account step moves the kept session in place
(POST /api/public/purchase/retainer-selection). The server half (gate, skip path, connect path's
RetainerPending -> RetainerConsented swap with credentials intact, resume incl. readConsentSkipped, selection
matrix, entitlement + portal handoff) is covered live against Postgres by
artifacts/api-server/src/routes/account-first-retainer.live-db.test.ts. RET1-RET4 (#1379 slug preselection) asserted
the buying screen on arrival, which no longer exists before an account; they were replaced by RET1 below. The
#1379 slug mapping (RET_TIERS keyed by catalog slug) is unchanged code.
Git #4339 (sessionTag 4339-rehydrate): the Retainer stored-session reload rehydrate #4339 added was retired by
#4383 — with every product account-first, a returning buyer resumes by signing in (#4377) and a stored id alone
is never trusted. The two apiTests remain as plain consent-status guard coverage.
Git #4377 (sessionTag 4377-account-first): Monitoring runs account -> read consent -> tier & pay -> portal, with the
same identity step and pre-consent door as Packs (#4378). The consent URL is refused server-side (409
account_required) until the session's account has a password and MFA. Tier/seats move on the session in place
(POST /api/public/purchase/monitoring-selection; seats lock once connected). A returning buyer signs in on /buy
(real /auth/login + MFA challenge) and GET /api/public/purchase/resume returns their own session. The sign-in,
consent and resume path needs a real TOTP and a Microsoft consent this harness cannot drive; it is covered by
artifacts/api-server/src/routes/account-first-purchase.live-db.test.ts. The old MON1-MON3 (#1317) connect-first
assertions described an order that no longer exists and were replaced.
Git #4469 (sessionTag 4469-tier-first): Monitoring reordered to account -> select tier -> connect -> pay -> login.
After the account, the Select tier step (tiers, seats, 'Continue with <tier>' = buy-tier-continue) writes the
selection onto the session; only then is the connect card offered (tier frozen, buy-tier-change until connected),
and terms + pay render only after the tenant is connected. Server-side the tier now locks at connect exactly like
seats: POST /api/public/purchase/monitoring-selection returns 409 tier_locked for a changed slug on a connected
session, so the consent-time scan's package is the one paid for (#4407). 'Login' is the existing done stage's
portal handoff (single-use token, auto sign-in on the account created first), not a second authentication. The
post-account steps need real TOTP + Microsoft consent; the lock is covered by account-first-purchase.live-db.test.ts
(step 4: seats_locked, tier_locked, unchanged re-send 200). The 4377/4383 steprail steps assert labels per product:
Monitoring's rail no longer carries 'Tier & pay' (asserted 'Select tier' instead); Retainer's still does.
Git #4378 (sessionTag 4378-account-first): Packs run account -> read consent -> packs/pay. /buy?product=pack
opens on the account step (data-stage='identity'): name/email/company mint the checkout session, then
#4374's pre-consent door (/api/public/purchase/pre-consent/*) proves the mailbox, creates the PackPending
account and enrolls MFA; only then does the buying screen (connect card, packs, pay) render. The old
PACK1/PACK2 buying-screen assertions and PACK6 (#1304 Coming soon badge, repointed to copilot by #4321) were
removed: they are unreachable without a real emailed code and real MFA enrollment. The #1304 drop-
unavailable-pack effect is unchanged code. The server half (pack-anchor gate matrix; PackConsented ->
Customer promotion at payment-confirmed; portal handoff for the account-first session) is covered
live against Postgres by artifacts/api-server/src/routes/public-purchase-account-first-pack.live-db.test.ts.
Git #1316 (sessionTag 1316-pack-flow): apiTests cover the fail-closed guards of the REAL pack
dry-run/execute/run-status endpoints (public-purchase-packs.ts). The paid-session happy path
needs a real paid+consented checkout session and REAL Graph reads/writes, so it is exercised by

Marketing rebuild Part 10. Recreated from Design/design_handoff_marketing/Marketing Buy.dc.html
into artifacts/shane-mccaw-consulting/src/marketing/pages/Buy.tsx (route /buy, already wired in
App.tsx by the Part 0 scaffold). All prices/tiers/pack data live in marketing/data/buyCheckout.ts,
not inline in the .tsx (no-hardcoding rule); pack names+prices are re-used from the canonical
quickStartPacks.ts fixture.
SCOPE — the deterministic, no-timer assertions that prove each product's own checkout rule:
MONITORING (gated): /buy?product=monitoring&seats=250 renders the 'Connect first' heading, the
read-only connect card, and a pay button reading 'Connect your tenant to continue'; the payment
fields are ABSENT until the tenant is connected (README: monitoring cannot be priced before the
tenant reports its seat count).
MONITORING (from a scan): /buy?product=monitoring&scanned=1 skips the connect step, shows the
connected card and the payment fields, prices on the real 1,240-seat tenant figure (Growth tier
= $9,920/mo), and the terms box gates the pay button ('Accept the terms to continue' -> 'Pay
$9,920 and start' once ticked) WITHOUT hiding the payment fields.
RETAINER (skippable, never gated): /buy?product=retainer&tier=essentials shows 'Pick your hours',
an optional Skip button, the payment fields (no connect gate), a $1,500/mo total, and the same
terms gate ('Pay $1,500 and start').
PACK (multi-select, summed): /buy?product=pack&packs=entra,ca sums to $998 (no /mo), reads '2
packs, one dry run', shows the payment fields, and gates on terms ('Pay $998 and continue').
PACK (not-yet-available gating, Git #1304, repointed at 'copilot' by #4321): /buy?product=pack&packs=entra,copilot
-- useQuickStartPackAvailability() cross-references PACKS against the real live `services`
table by name (no real row for Copilot Readiness today, per a direct query against local
Postgres run for #4321 -- MFA Enforcement, the pack this test originally targeted, now HAS a
real services row and had to be repointed); its option row renders a 'Coming soon' badge and
is dropped from the URL-preselected packSel once the live read resolves, leaving only Entra ID
Quick-Start selected ($799, not $1,298). This is the same gate /quick-start's own catalogue
uses, so a pack can never be paid for silently just because it lacks real backend fulfillment.
Only as stable as the live catalogue's current state -- if Copilot Readiness is later onboarded
as a real services row, repoint at whatever is genuinely not-yet-real then. This is also the
first live network call this otherwise-fixture-driven page makes; the 'NO backend' note below
now applies to every OTHER assertion in this manifest.
GIT #1317 (sessionTag 1317-integration): the post-payment flow is no longer simulated — every
stage transition is a real endpoint call (read consent popup+poll #1311, write consent #1312,
Stripe #1307/#1308, code/password/MFA #1310, monitoring scan kickoff riding set-password #1314,
portal auto-login handoff #1313/#1315, pack dry-run/execute #1316). Consequences asserted here:
contact fields render pre-connect for every product (the consent URL is minted against a session
created from them), ?scanned=1 no longer fabricates a connection or a fake 1,240-seat price, and
packs surface the REQUIRED read-consent connect card before payment. The paid happy path (real
Microsoft consent, real Stripe charge, real emailed code, real TOTP enrollment, real portal
auto-login, real pack dry-run/execute) cannot run from fixture-free manifest steps — it was
exercised in the #1317 session via a full Playwright UI E2E per product against this exact code
(see artifacts/api-server/_tmp_1317_e2e.mjs): Monitoring 19/19, Retainer 16/16, Pack 23/23, with
the pack execute reaching a REAL Graph write refused 403 by the write app's missing directory
permission (Azure-side, Shane To-Do on #1317).
DEPLOYED-ORIGIN CAVEAT (same class the sibling marketing manifests carry): this asserts against
{{DEPLOY_URL}}, which only reflects the new marketing site — and this page — once that site is
redeployed. Until the Part 0+ rebuild is the deployed frontend, /buy resolves to the old site's 404
fallback and these steps fail on that ground alone, not on a page defect. lastVerifiedAgainstCommit
is PENDING for that reason; the code itself is verified green locally as noted above.
